Scene 1 · Plate + overlay
Write songs the way you play.
Orange + paper fiber are baked into a single image with pigment running past the top and right edges — no painted border. Teal is a separate CSS overlay at the bottom-left using the existing wash-teal.webp asset, so its position can shift independently as the viewport changes. The diagonal between the two corners stretches or compresses to fit.
Scene 2 · Clean content
Most sections look like this.
No paper, no washes. Just cream, generous negative space, and one small note floating in the margin as a typographic rhythm mark — the way a music editor treats a coda sign. This is the default treatment for 80% of the page.
Scene 3 · Paper as accent
Texture, deliberately placed.
When paper does appear outside the hero, it's because something needs to feel like a physical object — a notebook page, a dedication card, a printable PDF preview. Not as wallpaper. As a prop.
Offline · Export · Print
Export clean PDFs for the stage.
Chord charts, lyric sheets, setlists — laid out on the same paper your song lived on the whole time. No pixels, no subscription, no round-trip through the cloud.
Scene 4 · Accent-only
One corner wash. That's it.
For most section breaks, a single off-canvas wash at a quiet opacity is enough. It stains the corner warm without asking for attention. No paper, no notes cluster, no competing decor.

Scene 5 · Corner mood blobs
Mostly off the page, barely touching.
Each mood blob sits almost entirely beyond the frame — only a soft corner lobe of pigment reaches into the scene. The four corners use four distinct assets (orange-b / teal-a / orange-a / teal-b) so adjacent corners never share pigment or shape, and each diagonal carries one denser piece and one quieter one for balanced weight. Visible pigment stays far enough from the scene center that nothing stacks or compounds into muddy overlaps.
Scene 6 · Horizontal drift
A quiet stain behind the words.
The drift variant sits centered behind copy at reduced opacity — horizontal cloud form with asymmetric weight, so it reads as atmosphere rather than a circle. Mirror it with scaleX(-1) for the opposite weighting without generating a second asset.
